pr_semantic_analysis.change_summary: The user creation flow was changed so that errors occurring in the post-creation step (specifically, the AfterCreate callback which enqueues a verify-email task) no longer cause the overall user creation transaction to roll back. Instead, the user row is committed regardless, and any AfterCreate error is captured separately and surfaced as a logged warning without failing the CreateUser API call.

behavior_changes.description: User creation now commits the user record even if the AfterCreate step (enqueuing verify-email tasks) fails. Such failures are logged but do not cause the CreateUser API to fail.
evidence: In CreateUserTx, the AfterCreate error is assigned to AfterCreateErr in the result and not returned to avoid rolling back the transaction.
In Server.CreateUser, AfterCreateErr is logged as a warning but does not cause the API call to fail.
The test case TaskDistributionFails asserts that even on distribution failure, user creation succeeds without error.

important_symbols.reason: Core transaction method modified to decouple AfterCreate errors from transaction rollback behavior.
API layer that surfaces the decoupled post-creation error as a logged warning without failing the request.
Test coverage added to explicitly verify that user creation succeeds despite AfterCreate failures.

investigation_hints.description: Examine transaction boundaries in user creation and ensure AfterCreate logic is correctly isolated to avoid transaction rollback.
Investigate API boundary behavior to ensure proper error visibility and logging without degrading API responsiveness.

local_risks: Potential silent loss or delayed recovery from AfterCreate failures since errors do not block user creation.
Invariants assuming AfterCreate always succeeds may be violated (e.g., users expected to receive verification emails immediately).
Logging is the only notification on AfterCreate failure; if logs are missed, failure may go unnoticed.
Test mocks (particularly for AfterCreate and task distribution) must accurately simulate failure modes to avoid false confidence.
uncertainties: Whether callers or downstream systems depend on AfterCreate success synchronously—this is not evident from the diff.
Effects on user experience from delayed or missing verification emails due to failed AfterCreate tasks are not shown.
Whether any retries or compensating workflows exist for AfterCreate failures is unknown from the supplied context.
Extent to which the logging approach fits broader monitoring and alerting policies cannot be established here.
